conflict_synopsis.core_view: Canadian headline inflation and BoC energy pass-through risk are underpriced versus a historically extreme CA-US yield discount after a fully priced Fed hike.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Next Canadian CPI or BoC communication converts the energy pass-through warning into a less-easy CA policy path.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: Canadian core stays near 2% and labor keeps cooling, so the cheap CA-US spread is revealed as warranted easier policy.

remit: currencies where inflation and policy risks are underpriced to the upside
stance_summary: CAD inflation and BoC restraint are underpriced versus a historically extreme CA-US yield discount after a fully anticipated Fed hike.

catalysts: Next Canadian CPI print that lifts headline or core via energy/food pass-through
Subsequent BoC communications that convert the minutes' pass-through warning into a delayed-easing or hike-bias reaction function
Persistence of crude near the retained $110 shock-absorber regime
US data that stops adding US-only front-end premium
evidence_refs: rollup:BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through risk
trade.invalidation: BoC communication or incoming Canadian CPI shows energy failing to lift headline/core while labor deterioration continues, so the CA-US discount is revealed as warranted easier policy rather than underpriced inflation risk.
trade.mispricing: CA-US 2Y at -140bp (3.8th one-year percentile) and CA-US 10Y at -111bp (0.20th one-year percentile) assume BoC can stay far easier than the Fed because core is near 2%; that ignores stuck 3% headline CPI, BoC minutes flagging energy pass-through, Canadian activity/consumer still above 52, and crude near $110.
principal_risks: Core staying near 2% and wages/employment continuing to cool
Saudi/Oman workaround collapsing the oil tail
Paying 140bp of US-CA 2Y carry while the reprice is delayed
Further Fed tightening that widens CA-US again
trade.thesis: Canadian headline inflation persistence plus BoC energy pass-through risk are underpriced relative to a historically extreme CA-US yield discount after a fully anticipated Fed hike, so CAD policy restraint should reprice higher and USDCAD lower.
why_now: Fed 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% was greater-than-90% priced and is now known; residual hawk risk has migrated to currencies still priced for easier policy.
BoC minutes already flag higher energy pass-through while August CPI held at 3% and CA-US spreads cheapened further over the month.
Energy shock absorbers remain weak and the last24 desk says the shock is constraining the global easing impulse.
